A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RNA representation study. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and can be matched across the reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original RNA prediction experiments, pooling comparisons, data and label scarcity tests, and sequencing-noise experiments in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and reports additional foundation-model and 3D-model evaluations in Table 1 and Appendix I.

M1.justification: v1 introduces nucleotide pooling for EGNN and SchNet; v2 additionally constructs a nucleotide-pooled FastEGNN variant (Section 4.1, Table 1). This is a limited architectural adaptation using the existing pooling strategy. The proposed ensembles and higher-degree architectures remain future work.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate COVID, Ribonanza-2k, Tc-Riboswitches, and Fungal on the same prediction tasks and data-scarcity, partial-label, robustness, and OOD-noise scenarios. Appendix D in v2 elaborates existing tasks rather than introducing new evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds RNA-FM, SpliceBERT, FAENet, DimeNet, GVP, and FastEGNN, including a pooled FastEGNN variant. FastEGNN also joins the existing data-scarcity, partial-label, and noise comparisons. This substantially broadens the evaluated sequence and 3D comparator families.

E3.justification: The reported SNR filtering, 70:15:15 splits, MCRMSE metric, Optuna selection, parameter and memory limits, training-data fractions, label fractions, and mutation probabilities remain unchanged. The added task descriptions do not report a revised evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: v2 extends the pooling ablation to FastEGNN and examines its behavior under the existing data, label, and noise variations. These extend established analyses to another architecture. The attention-map analysis, structural-prediction comparisons, and runtime/memory analysis are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations across five random data splits. The new result rows follow this existing practice; no new confidence intervals, significance tests, or changed repetition counts are reported.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial numerical evidence in Table 1 and FastEGNN results across ten appendix tables. For example, new COVID MCRMSE entries include RNA-FM at 0.591 ± 0.081 and SpliceBERT at 0.588 ± 0.077. Matched results for the original models remain unchanged; these are additions, not same-model performance improvements.

T1.justification: Neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs. The metric formula and training-subset definition are retained. The expanded task descriptions and discussion of equivariant expressivity add explanations, not new formal derivations or assumptions.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same contributions and headline claims about geometric information, approximately 12% error reduction, data efficiency, and noise sensitivity. The conclusion preserves the same findings; its additional architecture suggestions concern future work.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the foundation-model results, hypothesizes that FastEGNN's virtual-node initialization conflicts with RNA's sequence prior, and distinguishes high-noise behavior from lower-noise conditions. Appendix E adds limitations concerning untested higher-degree equivariant models and elaborates noise-aware ensembling, while retaining the central interpretations.

D1.justification: The new reproducibility statement explicitly promises release of datasets and benchmarking environments alongside code, extending v1's code-release promise. This remains a future commitment without an access location. Hardware, implementation-source information, and Table 5 are unchanged, and configurations for the added baselines are not supplied.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands engagement with foundation-model benchmarking, spectral GNNs, and advanced equivariant architectures, especially in Section 4.1 and Appendix E. It adds literature supporting the new comparators and explaining untested alternatives, while dropping Franke et al. (2022). The original first-systematic-study positioning remains.

P1.justification: The lengthy model catalogue moves from Section 2.3 to Appendix B. New structured explanations of all five tasks substantially expand the exposition in Appendix D, alongside an architecture-discussion appendix and ethics and reproducibility statements. This reorganizes the supporting narrative substantially, although most main-text prose is retained.

P2.justification: Table 1 expands and separates pooled from unpooled 3D models; several appendix tables gain FastEGNN rows. Figures 2, 3, 5, and 6 gain its curves and revised legends. Figure 2 corrects the Fungal panel label, Figure 3 corrects the labeling-fraction axis, and Table 2 adds task levels. Existing displays are otherwise retained within the new conference layout.

improvement.justification: The broader comparisons address v1's limited sequence and 3D comparator coverage, while the added limitations and corrected figure labels improve interpretation. However, the new baselines lack documented configurations and foundation-model adaptation procedures, and Table 5 still covers only the original models. The revision therefore provides useful additional evidence and clarity without establishing a substantial overall quality gain.
